parsed.explanation: Same-sex conduct is criminalised (life imprisonment on the mainland; gross indecency 1–5 years; up to five years for sex between women in the semi-autonomous jurisdiction), and the record shows this lever actually used against gender-nonconforming people: the 2018 Dar es Salaam 'witch hunt' with a regional commissioner's committee, forced anal examinations and torture, and a 2013 documented police rape and beating of an LGBT detainee. A June 2024 abduction and mutilation of a transgender activist drew only international condemnation, not domestic prosecution. No working remedy exists for trans victims; police are documented perpetrators. Against this: no explicit cross-dressing or gender-presentation offence, no capital charging for identity, and no documented border, registration or facility rule aimed at trans visitors. Severity if outed is high; the visitor-facing administrative exposure is undocumented rather than protective.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border rule documented; a passport marker mismatched to presentation would be handled by officers in a state with documented hostility to gender nonconformity, with no documented safeguard.
entry_documents.interaction: Border stage feeds into the same gross-indecency enforcement machinery documented domestically; no separate visitor screening regime is evidenced either way.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented police custody abuse of LGBT detainees (2013: rape with objects, caning), the 2018 city 'witch hunt' with forced anal examinations and a 17-member committee to identify and punish homosexuals, and internet scouring for videos.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; no visitor-specific custody protocol or complaint mechanism shown to operate.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An identity or document discrepancy can route a traveller into the same investigative/custody chain; no evidence of separation between immigration and morality enforcement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented rule on placement of trans detainees by birth sex or on facility access for trans visitors in this record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unresolved whether subnational and national custodial regimes differ; both criminalise the underlying conduct.

care_services.exposure: 2017 deportation of HIV/AIDS organisation staff for 'promoting homosexuality' disrupted services; enforcement of non-discrimination commitments is not established.
care_services.protection: Paper only: 2010 nursing regulations, 2013 family-planning guidelines and 2017 respectful-care guidelines bar withholding care based on sexual orientation.
care_services.interaction: Policy text does not reach a visitor whose presentation triggers suspicion; staff discretion is the operative gate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Criminalisation of same-sex conduct with life imprisonment available; gross indecency 1–5 years; subnational statute penalises sex between women up to five years; declining speech and assembly freedom; LGBTIQ websites blocked.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Media council code bars hate speech on sexual orientation; broadcast hate-speech rules; online hate-speech regulations repealed in 2020.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hate-speech paper rules sit alongside active blocking and prosecutorial weaponisation documented by a 2024 human-rights report.

minors_guardians.exposure: Gross-indecency age thresholds (absolute below 12; under-18 and marriage distinctions) plus a criminalised environment; no youth-specific protective healthcare provision beyond age-inclusive family-planning counselling language.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian accompanying a trans minor faces the same enforcement climate; document mismatch at hotels or checkpoints would out both.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: June 2024: transgender activist abducted by 12 men, beaten, ears cut; no domestic prosecution or remedy documented. 2024 report describes escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment and violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: UN Human Rights Office condemnation and calls for action; constitutional equality guarantees invoked but not shown enforced.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No gay venues; informal meeting places only; police response to trans victims is undocumented or documented as perpetrator.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented working remedy for trans or LGBT victims; complaints risk further exposure; aid withheld by a neighbouring jurisdiction over the crackdown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Foreign ministry disavowal of the 2018 crackdown; some named activists publicly back LGBTQ rights.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: International condemnation has not produced domestic accountability; the deterrent operates only at the diplomatic level.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia criminalises gender presentation itself, arrests visitors at transit checks and documents capital charging. Here there is no presentation offence and no capital case; criminalisation targets conduct, and arrests of visitors are undocumented. This dossier sits materially above that anchor, though both show lethal-severity custody abuse.

Vellandra applies a universal visitor register with routine refusal and no remedy — inescapable, but ending in exclusion rather than violence. Here no visitor-facing border regime is documented, yet the severity if drawn into enforcement (anal examinations, custody rape, mob mutilation with impunity) is far higher. Lower probability, much higher severity: net below.

Kestrel Isles has documented secondary screening and refusal, but written decisions, an appeal desk and consular notification that sometimes operate. Here no working remedy or appeal is documented for the class of person at risk, and the state is documented as perpetrator. Materially below.

Meridia's police routinely extort and briefly detain trans travellers, but sentences are short, flogging abolished, and a legal clinic occasionally wins compensation. This dossier has less trans-directed police routine but documents custody sexual torture, a state-announced witch hunt, and an unprosecuted mutilation. Comparable tier, slightly below on severity.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a live criminalisation statute with documented use of that lever against gender-nonconforming people: forced anal examinations, a publicly announced municipal witch hunt, and torture in police custody, with police as perpetrators rather than protectors. The single most recent trans-specific event — the June 2024 abduction and mutilation of a transgender activist — produced only international condemnation, evidencing impunity. Non-discrimination language in nursing and family-planning guidance is paper, unenforced. Offsetting factors are real but thin: no gender-presentation offence, no capital charging for identity, no documented visitor-facing border or registration rule, and diplomatic pushback. Severity if outed is high and recourse is absent; visitor-facing exposure is undocumented rather than demonstrated, which keeps the score above the outright-persecution anchors but well within the high-risk band.
